title: Exact selection of a toric-code vison crystal in a flux-conditioned Kitaev model
abstract: We construct an exactly solvable extension of the spin-$1/2$ Kitaev honeycomb model in which conserved $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fluxes determine not only the signs but also the connectivity of nearest-neighbor Majorana hopping. At a tuned loop point, hopping survives only across opposite-flux plaquettes, so every vertex has active degree zero or two and the matter Hamiltonian fragments in each flux sector into independent Majorana rings and isolated zero modes. Exact ring spectra and bond counting then bound the matter energy over all local flux configurations and all four Wilson-loop sectors, and split it exactly into a frustrated triangular-lattice Ising term, whose extensively degenerate ground states are the fully packed loop coverings, and a non-negative Majorana residual. On admissible commensurate tori, the residual selects precisely the three translation-related $2/3$-vison crystals, which saturate the bound, and an exact fermion-parity identity shows that for antiferromagnetic coupling their vacua also survive projection, making them rigorous ground states of the spin model. Within a single crystal, a depth-one local unitary then maps the ground space onto that of a sheared square-lattice toric code, giving fourfold topological degeneracy. The model thus realizes exact nonperturbative gauge-matter feedback: the flux fixes where the Majorana fermions may move, and their zero-point energy selects in return a topologically ordered vison crystal with spontaneously broken translation symmetry.
summary: This work analyzes an extended Kitaev honeycomb model to show how conserved Z2 fluxes dictate the connectivity of Majorana hopping. By tuning the model to a specific 'loop point,' the system exhibits exact gauge-matter feedback, leading to the selection of a stable, topologically ordered 2/3-vison crystal. This crystal structure is shown to possess the logical properties of a sheared square-lattice toric code.
main_problem: To investigate how conserved Z2 fluxes can control not only the signs but also the connectivity of nearest-neighbor Majorana hopping in the Kitaev honeycomb model, and whether this leads to a non-uniform flux ground state via gauge-matter feedback.
main_result: The model realizes exact nonperturbative gauge-matter feedback, selecting a topologically ordered 2/3-vison crystal that possesses fourfold topological degeneracy within a single crystal.
method: The analysis involves constructing an exactly solvable extension of the Kitaev model, analyzing the effective Majorana bilinear coupling in flux sectors, and using local unitary transformations to map the ground space onto a sheared square-lattice toric code.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 Kitaev honeycomb model, extended to include flux-dependent hopping. The Hamiltonian is analyzed by examining its fragmentation into independent Majorana rings and zero modes within specific flux sectors.
key_observables: Topological degeneracy (fourfold), ground state energy density, and the selection of the 2/3-vison crystal structure.
important_parameters: The analysis is critically dependent on tuning the system to a specific 'loop point' where hopping survives only across opposite-flux plaquettes.
main_assumptions: The analysis of the global flux competition and the selection of the crystal is specific to the fine-tuned loop point; away from this point, only sector-specific bounds are established.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates plaquette and orientation conventions, showing how the loop point forces active bonds only where adjacent plaquettes have opposite fluxes. Figure 6 illustrates the 2/3-vison crystal on a torus, showing flux-free plaquettes and the paths of the dual strings T1 and T2.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the flux-dependent hopping mechanism, analyzing the system at the critical 'loop point' where the matter Hamiltonian fragments, deriving the energy bound from loop coverings, and finally confirming the topological structure by mapping the ground space to a known toric code model.
why_interesting: The explicit realization of gauge-matter feedback—where the flux pattern dictates the fermion movement, and the resulting zero-point energy selects the flux pattern—provides a concrete, solvable model for understanding topological order in strongly correlated magnetic systems.
